What “review prompt on the product page” actually means

Apple’s in-app review API runs after install — the system sheet with stars and “Write a Review.” Buyers on the China App Store decide before they tap Get based on what your listing shows: title, subtitle, description, keywords, and screenshot gallery overlays. Many indie apps dedicate a gallery frame to the rating flow — a pre-prompt screen, the native star sheet, or marketing copy like “Love the app? Leave a review.” Those overlay lines and the listing body that mentions feedback are Connect fields we rewrite. They are not the same as calling requestReview() in Swift or replying to user reviews in App Store Connect.

  • Listing fields (in scope) — zh-Hans title, subtitle, description, keyword notes, screenshot overlay captions that name the review prompt, star rating sheet, or feedback ask
  • System review sheet (out of scope) — the native “Rate [App Name]” dialog Apple controls; its strings come from the OS, not Connect listing fields
  • requestReview() timing (out of scope) — when and how often your app triggers SKStoreReviewController; requires Xcode changes, not listing paste
  • App Review replies (out of scope) — responses to published user reviews in Connect; a different workflow entirely

Better zh-Hans listing copy helps Chinese players and utility users understand that you welcome feedback before install. It does not replace review-prompt engineering, custom pre-prompt UI inside the binary, or review-management retainers.

Why review-prompt marketing stalls on the China storefront

Western indie teams often ship review prompts early — after a milestone, on second launch, or from a settings toggle. The US listing gets polished; the zh-Hans row stays empty or mirrors English. On the China storefront, that gap shows up in predictable places:

  • English star sheet on screenshots — overlay says "Rate this app" or "Write a review" while the capture shows Chinese numerals and a zh-Hans app UI underneath
  • Pre-prompt copy untranslated — screenshot highlights "Enjoying the app?" and "Tap a star" with no zh-Hans equivalent in description or overlays
  • Description mentions reviews in English slang — "leave us a quick review", "rate us on the App Store", "your feedback helps" with no Chinese phrasing for 评分, 评价, or 留言
  • Keyword field ignores feedback intent — players search 好评, 用户评价, or app category + 评分; English keyword paste wastes the 100-character field
  • False social proof temptation — teams want to paste "4.8 stars" or "10k reviews" into listing copy; we do not invent ratings or counts — ever

These are public listing problems — not StoreKit bugs. Fixing them is copy you paste into App Store Connect, not a new build (unless you choose to re-export screenshots with updated overlay art yourself).

Review-prompt screenshot captions Chinese buyers expect

Productivity, utility, and lifestyle apps often dedicate one gallery frame to the feedback flow — a pre-prompt, the system star sheet, or a settings toggle that opens reviews. Overlay lines on those frames should name the feature in plain zh-Hans, not reproduce English dashboard labels:

  • Star sheet frame — describe the action: "轻触星星为应用评分" instead of "Rate this app" with no context
  • Pre-prompt frame — state the ask clearly: "喜欢这款应用？欢迎留下评价" — not vague "Enjoying the app?" floating on art
  • Settings path frame — if the screenshot shows a review toggle in settings, caption should say 设置中可前往 App Store 评价, not "Request a review" alone
  • Match caption to capture — if the screenshot shows three filled stars, the overlay should describe 评分 not 五星好评 guaranteed
  • No invented stars — we do not add "4.9★" or "万千用户好评" unless your English source already makes a verifiable claim you stand behind; we never fabricate averages or review counts

AppLocale includes review-prompt overlay lines in the screenshot caption deliverable when your gallery uses them. We do not redesign or re-export PNG assets — you paste overlay text into Connect or your design tool.

Keywords and description lines for review-aware listings

The review prompt is a retention feature, not a genre. Chinese search intent still starts with what the app is, then narrows to quality signals:

  • Category anchor first — 笔记, 番茄钟, 记账, 健身, 冥想; review vocabulary supplements, not replaces, core nouns
  • 评价 and 评分 — use when your listing honestly invites feedback; do not keyword-stuff "好评如潮" without basis
  • Description scope lines — plain zh-Hans bullets on how users can leave feedback (via in-app prompt or App Store) without promising more reviews
  • No fake social proof — repeating star counts, "#1 rated", or review totals you cannot verify violates both our scope and App Store metadata accuracy expectations

For the long description field specifically, see our description guide. AppLocale packs feedback vocabulary into keyword notes and description where Connect limits allow — we document rationale; we do not promise any term ranks on page one or that Chinese copy generates more reviews.

Why machine translation fails on review-prompt listings

  • Literal "Write a review" → "写一个评论" when Chinese App Store habits prefer 撰写评价 or 留下评价
  • "Enjoying the app?" translated as stiff 您正在享受应用程序吗？ — unreadable on a screenshot overlay
  • Star sheet captions that preserve English "Tap to rate" on art targeting zh-Hans buyers
  • Description promises "help us get to 5 stars" — sounds like astroturfing to Chinese readers
  • LLM invents review counts or star averages not in your English source
  • Review-prompt copy conflated with IAP tier names or Game Center achievement titles in the same paragraph
